verdict.root_cause: At 20:52:55 platform-automation pushed an image-reference update on the ad service to an ad-hotfix tag [tr_451a0f2a493a], and one second earlier the running ad JVM logged a complete, orderly gRPC shutdown and then went permanently silent — no startup, bind or listen lines ever follow through window close [tr_ee1f8a8e0866]. The replacement artifact never came up. Frontend traces show the consequence: the lone error chain terminates at frontend's outbound gRPC call to ad GetAds, a childless leaf failing in ~1ms, i.e. a connection-level refusal rather than ad-side logic or a timeout [tr_a84d740b0da4]. Frontend has no change of its own to blame [tr_d029746e7b7d]. The artifact running on ad is not one that serves traffic.
verdict.reasoning: The image flip at 20:52:55 and ad's graceful shutdown at 20:52:54 coincide to the second, and nothing restarts afterward [tr_451a0f2a493a, tr_ee1f8a8e0866]. The caller-side trace confirms no ad process accepted the call — no server child span — and the ~1ms failure distinguishes this from process_freeze and network_partition, which hang callers, and from dependency_latency, since all sampled traces finish in 4-47ms [tr_a84d740b0da4]. The orderly shutdown with no OOM, heap or panic lines rules out resource exhaustion [tr_ee1f8a8e0866]. Ad's flat error ratio [tr_a851199a2db8] is consistent rather than contrary: a process that is gone emits no spans, so the ratio cannot move. Reverting to the pre-hotfix reference that ran cleanly for the preceding ~8.9 hours is the fix [tr_451a0f2a493a].
open_questions: No pod or container-state evidence was gathered: ImagePullBackOff, CrashLoopBackOff, or never-scheduled all produce this symptom and were not distinguished.
The ad metrics query covered a window ending ~18 hours before onset [tr_a851199a2db8], so its 'ad is not the origin' conclusion is not actually measured against the incident.
The ~5 minute gap between ad's shutdown at 20:52:54 and the 20:58:01 onset is unexplained, and the breadth of the 8-service blast radius is unaccounted for by the single error path found.

alternatives.root_cause: The ad pod was terminated by eviction or scale-down and never rescheduled for lack of cluster capacity, leaving zero serving replicas.
alternatives.why_not: The shutdown lands within one second of a recorded image change on the same service, which explains the termination without invoking cluster pressure; stays live only because scheduler state was never inspected.

alternatives.root_cause: The hotfix build starts but binds or advertises a wrong address/port, so connections are refused by a nominally running service.
alternatives.why_not: A started process would log startup and bind lines; ad produced no output at all after 20:52:54, and the change log records only image references, no config pushes [tr_ee1f8a8e0866, tr_451a0f2a493a].

proposal.expected_effect: Redeploying ad at the pre-hotfix image reference it ran before the 20:52:55 update should bring a serving process back. Observable as: (1) the `{service="ad"}` Loki stream resuming with JVM startup / gRPC bind-and-listen lines followed by the routine 'ad request received' traffic lines that stopped at 20:52:40 — the stream has been completely silent since 20:52:54; (2) frontend traces to ad GetAds acquiring a server-side child span from ad instead of terminating as a childless ~1ms leaf, and that error span class disappearing from sampled frontend traces; (3) frontend's per-dependency ad call error count returning to zero. The first of these is the primary check: if ad logs never resume, nothing else matters.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, five minutes after the recreate, the ad log stream is still empty of any startup/bind/listen line — that means the container is not starting for a reason independent of which tag is referenced (never scheduled, host resource exhaustion, registry unreachable for both tags), and the artifact-choice diagnosis is wrong. Also falsified if ad comes up and serves but the incident's alerts across the other seven services persist: the brief's own open questions flag that a single frontend→ad error path does not account for an 8-service blast radius, nor for the ~5 minute gap between the 20:52:54 shutdown and the 20:58:01 onset, so there may be a second, unobserved mechanism this action does not touch. A third falsifier specific to this evidence: the change log shows five applies and four reverts of this same tag by platform-automation over ~10 hours, so if the hotfix tag reappears on ad within minutes of the rollback, the controller is reconciling against us and the fix will not hold regardless of whether it was correct.
proposal.risk: If the real failure is pod/container-state rather than artifact choice — ImagePullBackOff, a resource-starved host, or a never-scheduled workload — this recreate spends the outage window on a no-op and delays the correct diagnosis; no pod or container-state evidence was gathered at all, which is the weakest point in this proposal. If the hotfix tag was shipped to fix a real ad-service defect, reverting reintroduces that defect once ad is serving again. And because platform-automation has been flapping this tag all day, a manual rollback may contend with the controller and produce a further restart cycle on ad, turning a static outage into an oscillating one.
proposal.blast_radius: ad only for the recreate itself. frontend is ad's inbound caller in this graph and is already seeing hard connection-level refusals on GetAds, so it absorbs no new harm from the recreate window; frontend-proxy and load-generator see it transitively through frontend. cart, checkout, product-catalog, product-reviews and recommendation have no edge to ad in the sampled traces and should see nothing — if they do change state when ad is recreated, that itself is evidence the dependency picture in this brief is incomplete.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on frontend and its proxy simultaneously affect the user-facing entry point, which cannot be dismissed. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alerts alone don't distinguish a frontend deploy from a downstream dependency problem.
